title: DO THIS with your STUDENT LOAN REFUND [Investment Opportunity]
description:
Since I paid down student loans in March 2020, I qualified for a student loan refund. 

Whether or not Biden's student debt relief plan goes through, the refund can still go to work for you. Make sure to NOT SPEND IT because the forgiveness portion hasn't been approved, so you may need to pay it back. 

As always, THANK YOU for your support and love. We wish you all the absolute BEST with building wealth and enjoying retirement. 

ABOUT US 
Greetings from the Biesingers! We are so happy you are here! We are a family of four sharing our financial freedom (FIRE) journey, including tips on how to build wealth, retire early, and retire abroad.

At age 21, we purchased our first real estate property and then became first-time landlords at age 22 as college students. We worked extremely hard to pay off my student debt. Doing so helped me graduate with my MBA completely student-debt-free! 

We have other diversified investments and are excited to share more with you in our channel. We have now hit Coast FIRE, allowing us to move abroad and semi-retire in Asia! 

SUBSCRIBE TODAY! 
If you enjoy our videos and find them helpful, please give us a like and subscribe! We post regular personal finance content and are excited to share our experiences and financial freedom journey with you!

DISCLAIMER 
The information shared includes our personal research, experience, and opinions regarding managing money, retiring abroad, and pursuing financial freedom, but we are not financial advisors.

When making your personal finance and retirement decisions, we highly recommend researching multiple sources and/or receiving advice from a licensed professional. 

Keep in mind that visa processes and requirements are subject to change. Please make sure to conduct your personal research, check official websites, and consider talking with a registered visa agent before making a decision. 

Also, if looking to retire abroad, please visit the place you desire to retire first to have a feel of whether it is a good fit. Everyone's lifestyles and preferences will vary. 

AFFILIATE DISCLOSURE 
Some of the links shared in this channel are affiliate links. We may earn a commission if you click through, purchase, and/or subscribe.

asr.full_text: My wife and I contacted our student loan provider shortly after the Biden Student Debt Relief program was first announced last year. We received a refund from our loan provider, but have been waiting to see if the forgiveness portion will eventually get passed or not. Regardless, the refund was just sitting in my bank account and not being very productive for me. So I had to make a decision. I'll jump more into that later. The most current update is that the Student Debt Relief Plan is still blocked. be in my life. Now, how should I return it to my mom or to myself, whatever that may lead to, because the moment I'm in her shoes and if she comes home and says no, then I'm just going to get out. But as soon as you get off your car, just go ahead and return it, and you're ready to go. That's awesome. Alright, that really was a very informative one. Thank you. Next up, we have a question from Chris from Colorado State. And it is, can the loan repayment freeze end the loan application period after applying for the forgiveness plan? Let us know in the comment section below. In this video I will share my wife and I's process for applying for a refund slash loan forgiveness and how it actually turned out to be a great investment opportunity for us and if you find today's video helpful please give us a like, share a comment, and subscribe for more. So I wanted to share with you a few brief details about the Bidense Student Debt Relief Program. Those with federal student loan balances on or before June 30, 2022 could potentially receive a refund up to $20,000. Loans dispersed after July 1, 2022 don't qualify and private loans do not qualify as well. Here are some more eligibility details from studentaid.gov. You can also visit the website for everything you need to know about eligibility. good news for my situation is that i had paid off loans during the pandemic i made payments since march 2020. i was then eligible for a refund next i want to share my exact application process for the refund and forgiveness parts my student loans were originally housed with navient but then moved to a company called advantageantage upon hearing the debt relief announcement I called Advantage to see if I was eligible for a refund it was pretty funny and interesting because they did not have a formal process yet but took down my request and put me on a waiting list after calling back and waiting a bit longer I eventually received a refund for a little over twenty thousand dollars since I previously had Pell Gr grants so i want to add an important note that i only receive the refund not the forgiveness part so technically the twenty thousand dollars is still owed as of right now but the good news is that i don't have any payments due and zero interest charges i then submitted the application for the forgiveness portion of the biden student debt relief program on studentaid.gov but as mentioned before it has been blocked and they are not accepting any more applications at this time here is a copy of the email i received saying i was approved for loan forgiveness but the pause had been extended with the debt relief plan continually getting blocked my wife and i realized it probably wasn't the best option to have that refund sitting in our regular old account instead. We could have it working harder for us by putting into a high-yield savings account. Doing so would increase our high-yield savings balance to about $40,000 and give us about $120 monthly and interest payments this is because our highest savings account is with city bank with an interest rate of over 3%. Although it may not seem like a lot of interest payments can really add up and we could have well over $700 by the time the refund amount we had of $20,000 is either forgiven or need to be paid back. But the nice thing is we need to keep the interest payments. So why a high yield savings account? First off, a high yield savings account is a special type of savings account that offers a higher interest rate than the traditional savings account. First off, a high yield savings account is a special type of savings account that offers a higher interest rate than a traditional savings account. This can really add up over time and Second, you can access the money immediately. Let's say Biden's loan forgiveness doesn't go through I'd still be able to quickly pull the funds out and pay off the debt it would take longer to pull the money out of a 401 or another another investment account. Not to mention it would be riskier to put that money in those types of investment accounts. When choosing a high owed savings account. It is important to compare the features and fees of each option to find the best fit for your needs. You can find high-yield savings accounts at both online and brick and mortar banks. Many online banks offer higher interest rates than traditional banks so it's worth considering an online option if you're looking for the best return on your investment a great place to get started with your savings account is cit or sit bank they offer very competitive rates with no monthly maintenance fees with their savings connect account you can earn 12 times the national average there There's no ATM fees and you have the convenience of banking online. Also, to put your mind at ease, they are FDIC insured and they currently, I just looked it up, they offer over 4% interest rate saving accounts. You can check them out using the link I provided in the description below. Now if you find yourself in the same boat where you have a refund sitting in your bank it may be a good idea to get it moved over to high yield savings account. Overall, it's considered very safe. I would definitely not recommend putting your refund into the stock market or somewhere with higher risk and volatility. Sorry crypto, maybe next time. This same principle goes for any extra money you just have lying around. Instead of keeping it in low interest regular savings account, move it on over to a high-yield savings account. To see my wife and I's cost of living and first month breakdown of expenses in China, check out this video here.
